findings.classification: conditional current source-backed first-admission candidate; historical F025 refinement, central decides ledger identity
findings.observation: Current BrowserCommand is internally tagged and OrbitForge stores raw f32 deltas. queue_json parses from_str, and a successfully queued and drained OrbitForge adds scaled delta_x to retained yaw. Both 6533 and 95e browser sources have the tagged raw-f32 shape, but differ in full bytes.
source_reasoning: The pinned serde derive source generates TaggedContentVisitor via deserialize_any, buffers non-tag fields as Content through __deserialize_content_v1; serde_core default delegates to deserialize_any and a source-wide text search found no serde_json de.rs override.

Without arbitrary_precision, numeric tokens route through parse_integer to ParserNumber::F64, and ContentVisitor retains F64; the generated tagged-struct map asks for each f32 field, ContentDeserializer dispatches the F64 to the f32 visitor, whose cast does not check finite representability.

With neither arbitrary_precision nor float_roundtrip, the registered POW10 source and integer/exponent logic show that a well-formed positive 1e100 token is finite as f64 but outside f32 range and casts to positive infinity. Subject to successful command decode/queue/drain, yaw receives that value. This is source reasoning, not an executed input.

When float_roundtrip is enabled, direct do_deserialize_f32 sets single_precision and takes the f32 lexical branch; the internally tagged buffering path instead begins in deserialize_any with single_precision false. The f64 lexical result was not independently proved for a particular input because its subordinate algorithms were not fully read. Thus, if the f64 lexical branch returns a finite value outside f32 range and arbitrary_precision is disabled, later Content-to-f32 cast can still overflow. Do not claim the active target enables either feature or that float_roundtrip necessarily protects tagged fields.

With arbitrary_precision, parse_any_number has a different String-backed internal numeric representation. Its outcome in this route is not assessed here. This string is dependency-internal number encoding, not automatically an application magic-string defect.
conditions: Well-formed tagged command reaches queue_json; its fields meet other decoding requirements; non-arbitrary_precision selected; observed source route and numeric assumptions hold; queue lock succeeds and queued command is drained. Caller capability, actual target features, inputs and runtime observations are unverified.

No general guarantee about every caller or degenerate/nonfinite vectors follows.

Normalized gnarling fields are raw f32 and relevant clamp/normalize operations occur in the examined code, but this bounded inspection has not established an actual supported nonfinite value or zero-direction producer, a failing result, or a universal admission policy.

No new product magic-string issue is asserted from dependency-internal arbitrary-precision numeric string. The browser command tag is a serialized schema discriminator with explicit typed variants, not proof every external producer or evolution policy is covered.

Current shoot seed maps to existing TreeShootId; no existing project type was proven to own finite signed browser deltas.
A finite signed angle delta, stored angle and clamp domain have different semantics; no claim that generic UnitInterval fits.
Finite-value admission and repeated yaw accumulation are separate conditions; link the latter to q50, avoid duplicate counts.
Tree polyline length and branch/direction relations require more than each f32 field. Shown three-point caller meets length precondition; general caller policy remains open.
Internally tagged serde buffering establishes the conditional f64-to-f32 path; lock checksums do not prove target feature selection or real input.
BrowserCommand encodes orbit deltas in a tagged variant; this bounded review does not establish enum ownership outside the shown route.
Seed-derived shoot and geometry/bake key are related identity authorities in existing q77/q80; this helper alone cannot prove conflicts or intended equivalence.
Old intrinsic operations and current libm/multiplication differ in source. No numeric, visual or replay equivalence was validated.
Current shrub seed -> TreeShootId -> append and terminal-segment identity are visible in separately read windows; downstream and actual supported producers remain bounded.

Serde derives serialize the command through generated tagged content; this analysis identifies behavior of relevant derive sources, not an argument to replace handwritten boilerplate or remove validation.
